Definition: from G4862 and G4717; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively):--crucify with.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says our old man is crucified with Christ, so the body of sin might be destroyed. He says it again in Galatians, personally this time: I am crucified with Christ, and the life I now live I live by faith in the Son of God. Matthew uses the same word for the thieves crucified with Jesus, which is the literal picture behind Paul's figure. The cross was never a solo event for the believer; we were there in Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that being crucified with Christ is the only honest answer to sin's power. I cannot beat it by trying harder, and I do not have to: my old self died with Him, and the life I live now is His life in me. That is why Paul can speak of freedom, not as a hope for later, but as a fact already true.
